title: Western Blot CTB
author: Arindam Naha
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bastieen

steps.title: Arrest Protein Synthesis and Translocation
steps.instruction: Stop protein synthesis and translocation in E. coli cultures grown up to 4 hours post-induction with 0.2% arabinose.

substeps.instruction: Mix bacterial cultures with an equal volume of translation-translocation halt cocktail (200 µg/ml chloramphenicol, 200 mM sodium azide, 9.5% ethanol).
Immediately incubate the mixture in an ice water bath for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Harvest and Prepare Cell Lysates
steps.instruction: Separate cells from the culture and disrupt them to obtain crude lysates.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the culture at 14,000 rpm for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Preserve the supernatants for CT-ELISA experiments.
Resuspend the pellets in TME buffer (20 mM Tris-Cl pH 8.0, 2mM β-mercaptoethanol, 1 mM EDTA), preferably using 1/10th the volume of the original culture.
Centrifuge the lysate at 13,000 rpm at 4°C for 15 minutes to remove unbroken cells.

steps.title: Quantify Protein and Load Gel
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration and load equal amounts onto the gel.

substeps.instruction: Measure the protein concentration of the crude cell lysates using the Bradford assay (BioRad, USA).
Mount equal amounts (≥80 μg) of protein samples onto a 15% SDS-PAGE.

steps.title: Probe and Validate Blots
steps.instruction: Transfer proteins to a membrane and probe with specific antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Probe blots with either classical CTB-specific monoclonal antibody (anti-Cla CTB, 1:5000) or anti-beta lactamase (anti-βla 1:500) antibody.
Stain a portion of the blot with Ponceau S staining solution (Sigma-Aldrich, St Louis, MO, USA) to validate equal protein transfer.

steps.title: Develop and Analyze Blots
steps.instruction: Visualize the protein bands and perform densitometric analysis.

substeps.instruction: Develop blots using West Pico Chemiluminescent Substrate (Thermo Scientific, Rockford, IL) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Visualize the blots in a ChemiDoc XRS+ system (BioRad, USA).
Perform densitometric analysis of band intensities using Multi Gauge software V2.3 (FujiFilm).
